data.narrative:
Fairmat operates in Robotics & Manufacturing at the Series B stage, having raised approximately €95M ($103M) to date. The valuation assessment draws from a peer set of nine comparable companies: one public comparable (277810.KQ) and eight private firms including Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, and Dexterity, all at identical stage and sector positioning.

Two triangulation methods apply to this analysis. Stage-progression methodology, using total raised as a proxy base of $27M and applying a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, implies a valuation of $51M. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same-stage comparables yields a median valuation of $1.8B, with the three-company sample (Generalist AI at $2.0B, Bedrock Robotics at $1.8B, Dexterity at $1.6B) establishing a range of $1.6B to $2.0B.

These methods produce a wide triangulated range of $44M to $2.0B (median $901M), reflecting material divergence between capital-efficiency signals and peer-market multiples. The stage-progression method anchors a conservative scenario; peer-median methodology incorporates market sentiment for the sector but relies on a limited sample of three companies. Key uncertainties include the relevance of public and private comparables to Fairmat's specific product-market positioning, variation in peer company burn rates and path to profitability, and whether current peer valuations reflect sustainable pricing or cyclical peaks in robotics funding.
